content:
The image shows a soybean leaf with a single circular to irregular lesion on the upper surface. The lesion has:
- A pale/gray-white necrotic center
- A distinct dark reddish-brown to purple-black border/margin
- Surrounding green leaf tissue appears healthy
- Small scattered dark specks elsewhere on the leaf
- No yellow halo visible

This lesion morphology — gray/tan center with reddish-brown to dark margins — is the classic hallmark of **Frogeye leaf spot** (caused by *Cercospora sojina*). The circular shape, gray center, and dark red-brown ring match the description exactly. Phyllosticta leaf spot has irregularly shaped tan lesions with purplish margins but tends to appear in the lower canopy under cool conditions and has a different shape. Septoria brown spot lesions are typically smaller, darker brown, and irregularly shaped without the distinct gray center. Bacterial blight shows angular, water-soaked lesions with yellow halos — not seen here.
